items.note: Prescription that in a town the prāsāda-temple be built before the dwellings (vāstu); canonical rule on temple precedence in town planning.
items.gloss: In the town, build the prāsāda-temple before the (other) vāstu dwellings.

items.note: Canonical (Samarāṅgaṇa-derived) rule distinguishing house and temple halls: an alinda-less śālā is 'praiseworthy in a devālaya'. Restored after a checker-crash workaround (QC follow-up).

items.note: Material taken from another vāstu must not be used in a prāsāda (temple), or worship will not take place there.
items.gloss: Material removed from one site must not be used in another; in such a prāsāda (temple) no worship occurs, and no householder dwells in such a house.

items.note: Defines the shadow of a prāsāda's śikhara as 'dhvaja-chāyā' and treats sunrise tree/flag shadows as censurable.
items.gloss: Tree-shadow and flag-shadow at sunrise are condemned; crossing the door they cause hunger, illness, quarrels. The shadow of a prāsāda's spire is called flag-shadow.

items.note: Images of condemned episodes from itihāsa-purāṇa are not desirable in houses but are proper in temples; canonical prescription on temple imagery.
items.gloss: Images (pictures/sculptures) of censured episodes from history and purāṇa are not desirable in houses; in temples they are proper.
